question: After a serious breach, what single credential do incident responders change — doing it a second time, not just once — so all counterfeit access proofs already handed out in the environment stop working immediately?
gold_facts: The krbtgt account password is reset twice during recovery
This invalidates every previously issued ticket, including forged Golden Tickets

question: What kind of server would a company put in a small branch office with weak physical security, so that even if someone stole it, most user secrets still wouldn't be exposed?
gold_facts: Holds a read-only copy of the directory database with a filtered attribute set
Has a per-device password replication policy
Designed for branch offices and untrusted locations

question: Why would logins throughout the whole office suddenly start failing right after someone adjusted the calendar/date setting on one machine by a small amount?
gold_facts: W32Time keeps clocks synced with the PDC emulator as the authoritative source
A skew exceeding 5 minutes breaks Kerberos authentication

question: Two accounts got created with overlapping login identifiers by mistake — why would that cause random ticket-based sign-in errors and break cloud identity syncing?
gold_facts: Each SPN/UPN must be unique forest-wide
Enforced by Windows Server 2012 R2+ domain controllers
Duplicate values cause Kerberos auth failures and break Entra ID sync

question: How do security teams structure admin accounts so that if someone's laptop login gets phished, the attacker still can't touch the servers running the whole company?
gold_facts: Separates administration into discrete tiers (forest/domain-wide, servers, workstations/users)
Designed so a compromise at one tier can't escalate to a higher tier

question: How does a cluster turn my raw application source into something actually running, without me writing a container recipe file myself?
gold_facts: Source-to-Image (S2I) is the default no-Dockerfile strategy
The output is pushed to an ImageStream
An ImageChange trigger drives the next rollout

question: I asked for some disk space for my app and it's just sitting there unfulfilled — what's the chain of objects supposed to hand it storage automatically?
gold_facts: A StorageClass triggers dynamic provisioning through a CSI driver
The claim gets bound to a matching PersistentVolume
Failure in this chain shows as the claim stuck Pending

question: What component keeps the low-level settings on every worker host identical, and what happens if someone edits a setting directly on one of those hosts by hand?
gold_facts: MachineConfig objects describe desired on-node OS/systemd/file state per pool
The Machine Config Operator applies them via the Machine Config Daemon
Drift from the rendered config marks a node/pool Degraded

question: If traffic to my app spikes, what watches resource usage and spins up more copies on its own, rather than making each copy bigger?
gold_facts: The HPA controller adjusts replica count based on observed CPU/memory/custom metrics against min/max bounds
It scales horizontally (more pods), not vertically
v2 adds per-direction scale-up/down tuning

question: Why does a packaged app that works fine on my laptop's local orchestration setup suddenly get blocked here, complaining it isn't permitted to launch with the top administrative user ID?
gold_facts: The default restricted-v2 policy runs containers as a random non-root UID
This is the most common reason a community image that works on plain Kubernetes fails

question: While a system is moving to a newer release, what should I check initially to see which infrastructure pieces haven't finished converging on the new build yet?
gold_facts: Status reports Available/Progressing/Degraded for each platform component
The Cluster Version Operator reconciles the whole set during install and upgrade
oc get co is the first triage stop

question: When I want to add a third-party extension to manage a database inside my cluster, what handles bringing in that add-on and keeping it current without me doing it by hand each time?
gold_facts: OLM manages Operators via CatalogSource/Subscription/InstallPlan/ClusterServiceVersion/OperatorGroup CRDs
It is distinct from the Cluster Version Operator, which has no Subscription object

question: My program takes a long time to boot and keeps getting killed and relaunched again and again before it's even finished loading — what setting is supposed to prevent that, and what are the two additional tests that determine whether it gets requests?
gold_facts: Three kubelet health checks exist: liveness, readiness, and startup
Startup delays the other two checks for slow-booting apps
Tuning fields include initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, and failureThreshold

question: How do I combine several physical cables between two switches into what looks like one faster pipe, and why might traffic still favor certain physical wires unevenly?
gold_facts: Bonds multiple physical links into one logical channel
Uses flow-based 16-bucket load balancing
LACP provides flow-based active/standby redundancy and must be enabled on both ends

question: Two boxes sitting on the same wire refuse to become neighbors — what set of timers and settings has to line up exactly before that relationship forms?
gold_facts: It is a link-state interior gateway protocol
Forming an adjacency depends on matched hello/dead/auth values
Cost is derived from a tunable reference bandwidth

question: In a large internal network, how do you avoid connecting every box directly to every other box just so paths propagate, and what stops a path from circling back to where it started?
gold_facts: Route reflectors scale iBGP without a full mesh by reflecting learned routes
Loop avoidance uses Originator-ID and Cluster-list
They honor only set ip next-hop on reflected routes

question: Why does it take my LAN about half a minute to recover after I unplug a redundant uplink, and which device in the topology gets picked as the reference point everyone else calculates distance from?
gold_facts: Convergence takes about 30 seconds across five port states
Election of the reference bridge is by lowest bridge ID
PVST+ interoperates with the Common Spanning Tree

question: Our resource server is returning invalid_dpop_proof for a chunk of API calls, and occasionally invalid_token too. What's going on and how do we fix it?
gold_facts: invalid_dpop_proof means the DBD proof structure is wrong: wrong typ, bad alg, missing claim, htu mismatch, wrong/missing ath, nonce mismatch, or signature failure
invalid_token means the token's cnf.jkt does not match the proof jwk thumbprint
the RS must require a DPoP header and must not fall back to accepting the token as a plain Bearer token

question: Token exchange is failing every single time with error=invalid_grant and the message 'PKCE verification failed'. What's wrong?
gold_facts: S256 encoding errors (wrong base64, padding, charset) produce error=invalid_grant 'PKCE verification failed' reproducibly on every token exchange
omitting code_challenge_method while sending an S256 hash makes the AS treat it as plain, so the comparison never matches, also producing invalid_grant
clients must never fall back to plain after an S256 failure

question: We see 'logout_token missing events/sub/sid' errors at our RP's backchannel logout endpoint, and separately users report they can log back in immediately after logging out. What's the cause?
gold_facts: 'logout_token missing events/sub/sid' happens when the RP rejects the token because the OP constructed it from the ID Token code path instead of a proper Logout Token
the Logout Token MUST NOT contain nonce and MUST contain an events member with http://schemas.openid.net/event/backchannel-logout
users re-authenticating immediately after logout indicates the refresh token was not revoked even though the session cookie was cleared

question: Browser console shows: "No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource" and our SPA appears to hang right after the OAuth redirect callback. What's broken?
gold_facts: this error occurs when the AS token endpoint is missing CORS headers, so the browser blocks the code-for-token exchange before it reaches the AS
the AS must send Access-Control-Allow-Origin on every browser-called endpoint: token, discovery, JWKS, revocation, introspection, and UserInfo
wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * combined with Allow-Credentials: true is hard-rejected by the browser

question: Our resource server keeps returning 401 invalid_token for mTLS-bound access tokens even though the client presents a valid cert. What are the likely causes?
gold_facts: invalid_token (401) from the RS usually means the cert thumbprint never matches, commonly from hashing PEM text instead of DER bytes, or the client cert not reaching the RS through TLS termination
the binding is carried in cnf.x5t#S256 = base64url(SHA-256(DER-encoded cert)) with trailing = padding omitted
the RS must NOT validate the cert's trust chain during the proof-of-possession check, only match the thumbprint exactly

question: We're getting redirect_uri_mismatch errors in production after tightening our AS config, and separately a pen-test flagged an open-redirect via authorization code theft. How are these related?
gold_facts: redirect_uri_mismatch / invalid_redirect_uri appears immediately when the AS enforces exact match but the submitted URI doesn't match; if the AS was previously lenient, tightening it surfaces this error in production
the AS must validate redirect_uri using RFC 3986 exact string comparison, not wildcard or prefix matching
if a registration used a wildcard or host-only URI, an authorization code or token can be delivered to an attacker-controlled URI

question: A refresh token request is returning invalid_grant on the very first use of the token (not the second). Is this expected rotation behavior or a problem?
gold_facts: invalid_grant is the correct error on the token endpoint when a rotated/consumed refresh token is replayed
if invalid_grant occurs on the *second* use of a token, rotation is working correctly; if it occurs on the *first* use, the token was already consumed, possibly by an attacker
when the AS detects replay of a consumed token, it SHOULD revoke the entire grant family, and legitimate clients should treat invalid_grant as session termination and redirect to re-authenticate

question: Introspection calls are returning 415 Unsupported Media Type from our AS, and separately we noticed our resource server code reads `scope` and `exp` from the introspection response without ever checking `active`. What issues does this create?
gold_facts: 400 Bad Request or 415 Unsupported Media Type occurs when introspection is called over GET or with a JSON body instead of POST with application/x-www-form-urlencoded
resource servers MUST check the active flag first before reading any other claim; skipping this check means revoked or expired tokens can still authorize API calls
when active is false the AS SHOULD NOT return any other claims, so relying on other fields without checking active is unsafe

question: A pen-test found that our API accepts a token with alg:none, and separately we saw an ID Token get replayed successfully against a protected API endpoint. How are these both JWT validation failures?
gold_facts: alg:none (and case variants) must always be rejected; a permissive verify() that honors the token's own alg header is an algorithm-confusion vulnerability that can allow auth bypass
JWT access tokens per RFC 9068 carry typ: at+jwt; resource servers must reject tokens with typ: JWT or missing typ, otherwise an ID Token from the same AS can be replayed as an access token
key separation between ID Tokens and access tokens is not a security boundary because the RS trusts any key published in the AS's JWKS

question: RHBK 26 two-site Active-Active deployment with sticky sessions ON and a shared external Data Grid cluster is throwing intermittent invalid_grant on POST /realms/<realm>/protocol/openid-connect/token with grant_type=refresh_token, worse under load. We suspected LB stickiness, Infinispan replication lag, or clock skew — which is it?
gold_facts: the root cause is architecture mismatch: RHBK's documented HA model is Active/Passive, not the Active-Active round-robin topology being run

sessions/clientSessions/offlineSessions/offlineClientSessions caches are NOT cross-site replicated -- only authenticationSessions, actionTokens, loginFailures, and work are synchronously replicated via Data Grid Cross-DC, so a cross-site refresh forces a synchronous DB read
the HA guide explicitly warns that deadlocks may occur in an active-active setup as entries are modified concurrently in both sites (the work cache uses NON_DURABLE_XA + FAIL failure policy)

question: We're seeing 'Windows can't create the object because the Directory Service was unable to allocate a relative identifier' and Directory-Services-SAM event 16657 on our RID master. What's happening and how do we recover?
gold_facts: event 16657 (ceiling hit) is logged on the RID master when pool allocation crosses the 90% consumed threshold, and msDS-RIDPoolAllocationEnabled is set to FALSE on CN=RID Manager$, blocking further issuance
to unblock, use LDP.exe to set MsDS-RidPoolAllocationEnabled = TRUE on the RID Manager$ object, but this only delays exhaustion of the hard limit
the default global RID pool is 2^30 (~1.07 billion) RIDs per domain, expandable to 2^31 via the irreversible 31-bit unlock (SidCompatibilityVersion=1)

question: Kerberos auth is failing across the domain with KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW / STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE citing time skew. What role and service should we check first?
gold_facts: Kerberos requires client, KDC, and target service clocks to be within 5 minutes of each other; exceeding that produces KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW
the PDC emulator FSMO role is the authoritative time source for the domain and should sync from an external NTP source; other DCs sync from the domain hierarchy (NT5DS)
the 5-minute window is not configurable and should not be widened -- fix the clock, not the tolerance

question: We're getting Event ID 2887 (unsigned LDAP binds detected) and Event ID 3040 (channel binding token mismatch) on our domain controllers. What do these mean and what's the remediation path?
gold_facts: event 2887 indicates unsigned binds were detected (client source logged); event 3040 indicates a channel binding token mismatch tied to an SSL/TLS certificate issue

the recommended migration path is: set signing to 'Negotiate signing' and channel binding to 'When supported' first, review 2887/3039 to enumerate non-compliant clients, then enforce 'Require signing' and 'Always' for channel binding
channel binding does not protect plain port-389 connections -- it only applies to SSL/TLS (LDAPS) sessions

question: Account creation is failing forest-wide with error code 8648 / 0x21C8 ERROR_DS_UPN_VALUE_NOT_UNIQUE_IN_FOREST, and separately LSASS CPU is spiking on our DCs. What's the connection?
gold_facts: Windows Server 2012 R2+ DCs enforce forest-wide uniqueness for SPNs and UPNs; duplicate UPN writes are blocked with error 8648 / 0x21C8 ERROR_DS_UPN_VALUE_NOT_UNIQUE_IN_FOREST
a duplicate SPN causes the KDC to be unable to resolve which secret to use for Kerberos mutual authentication, which is what drives excessive LSASS CPU on the DC
Event ID 2974 is logged listing the blocked value and up to 10 conflicting objects; in a mixed domain, writes processed by pre-2012 R2 DCs bypass the uniqueness check entirely

question: After restoring a Hyper-V snapshot on a DC we saw Event ID 2170 'Generation ID change has been detected'. Is this a problem, and what does it trigger?
gold_facts: Event ID 2170 is logged when a VMGenID mismatch is detected with no DCCloneConfig.xml present, triggering automatic safe restore: InvocationID reset, RID pool discarded, and SYSVOL non-authoritatively synced
safe restore compares the live driver value from vmgencounter.sys against the stored msDS-GenerationId attribute in NTDS.DIT on every boot and on snapshot restore
this process runs automatically with no administrator input, but changes made after the snapshot point that had not yet replicated out are permanently lost

question: On a DC without VM-GenerationID support, we're seeing Event ID 2095 'previously acknowledged USN, no corresponding change in invocation ID', and the registry shows Dsa Not Writable = 0x4. What happened?
gold_facts: on hypervisors without VMGenID support, snapshot restores cause USN rollback: the DC resumes with reused USNs and replication partners believe they are already up to date, so divergence is silent until an out-of-range USN is detected
Event ID 2095 fires and the Net Logon service is paused (quarantine); Dsa Not Writable = 0x4 in HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters is the forensic marker
undetected divergence can surface later as lingering objects (Event ID 1988) if the rolled-back DC's USN counter advances past the partner's high-water mark before replication resumes

question: Service logons are failing with SPN mismatches and our LDAPS connections are throwing certificate mismatch errors on machines whose primary DNS suffix doesn't match the AD domain name. What's going on?
gold_facts: a disjoint namespace exists when a domain member computer's primary DNS suffix does not match the DNS name of the AD domain it belongs to
LDAPS certificate Subject/SAN must cover both the AD domain name and the primary DNS suffix, or mismatches cause LDAP connection failures
SPNs registered against the AD domain name may not match service FQDNs in the disjoint zone, causing Kerberos auth failures even without a true SPN uniqueness violation

question: Clients are getting 'no logon servers available' and DsGetDcName is failing, with DNS Query Failures/sec climbing on the DC Locator (Client) perfmon counter set. Where do we look?
gold_facts: DC Locator is implemented by the Netlogon service via DsGetDcName, which resolves SRV records under _msdcs.<forest-root> via DnsQuery and confirms availability with a UDP LDAP ping
the DC Locator (Client), (DC), and (Netlogon) perfmon counter sets (Windows Server 2025+) expose Requests: Failures/sec, Average Success Latency, DNS Query Failures/sec, and Cache Hits/Misses per sec
if BlockNetBIOSDiscovery is disabled and no WINS server is present, DC location can silently fall back to broadcast-only, which fails across subnets

question: After a WAN partition, two DCs in different sites diverged (split-brain). Once the link came back we saw Event ID 1988 lingering-object warnings plus Kerberos PAC validation errors (Event ID 4768/4769 with failure codes) on a service using SPNEGO against AD. What's the right fix order?
gold_facts: the PAC signing errors are a downstream symptom of divergent directory state (inconsistent group/key state), not an independent failure -- fix replication first and PAC errors resolve automatically once directory state converges

Event ID 1988 (lingering object) indicates an object exists on one DC but was tombstoned on the other and the tombstone lifetime elapsed on the partner without it; Event ID 2095 indicates USN rollback/conflict

if Keycloak/RHBK authenticates via Kerberos/SPNEGO against AD, PAC validation errors will appear in Keycloak logs as authentication failures, but the root cause is the AD split-brain, not Keycloak -- fix AD first

question: repadmin /showrepl shows replication failures with error 1753 (endpoint mapper) and event 1396 in the Directory Service log between two sites. What's the likely cause?
gold_facts: most 'replication is broken' tickets are not the replication engine itself but a dependency failure: DNS resolution failure, time skew breaking Kerberos (1396/1753 errors), or lingering objects after a DC was offline past the tombstone lifetime

the KCC (Knowledge Consistency Checker) automatically builds and repairs connection objects between DCs; error 1753 (endpoint mapper) typically indicates broken IP connectivity or a firewall blocking TCP 135 / RPC dynamic ports between sites
replication and DNS health fail together because DC Locator needs healthy DNS to resolve the _msdcs SRV records that turn site membership into an actual DC connection

question: We in-place upgraded our DCs to Windows Server 2025 but they're still using the 8k page format for NTDS.dit and hitting the old ~1,200-value multi-valued-attribute ceiling. Why didn't they get 32k pages, and what's the risk if we enable the feature?
gold_facts: in-place upgraded DCs retain the 8k page format and are not auto-upgraded to 32k -- only a new promote (fresh installation or new replica) on Windows Server 2025 gets a 32k-capable database
enabling the 32k pages optional feature is irreversible except via full authoritative forest recovery, and after enabling it, only 32k-page backup media can restore a Windows Server 2025 DC

moving to full 32k mode is a forest-wide operation requiring all DCs on Windows Server 2025+ with a 32k-capable database, raised functional levels, no replication errors, and Enterprise Admins membership

question: Pods can't resolve <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local and `oc get co dns` shows the DNS ClusterOperator Degraded. Where's the fault likely to be?
gold_facts: the DNS Operator deploys and manages CoreDNS as a daemon set and configures the kubelet to point pods' /etc/resolv.conf at the CoreDNS Service; DNS Available becomes True once at least one CoreDNS daemon-set pod is Available and the Service has a ClusterIP
every Service gets *.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local resolution via this mechanism
Kubernetes caps the injected DNS search list at 32 entries / 2048 characters -- exceeding it truncates the list and can silently break short-name resolution

question: A pod is stuck CrashLoopBackOff, and separately a Route to a different (Running) pod is returning 503 from the router. Both have probes configured -- what's the likely misconfiguration in each case?
gold_facts: on liveness probe failure the kubelet kills and restarts the container -- pointing liveness at a deep/slow dependency causes healthy containers to be killed in a restart loop under load, producing CrashLoopBackOff

on readiness probe failure the kubelet does NOT restart the container, it removes the pod from the Service's endpoints so no traffic is sent to it -- this is the mechanism behind a Route/Service returning 503 for an otherwise-Running pod
kubectl describe pod events name which probe fired and why -- read that line first to determine whether the fix is a restart-loop or traffic-removal issue

question: We added a NetworkPolicy to a namespace and now expected traffic between two pods is being silently dropped. Separately, in another namespace a pod turned out to be reachable from a namespace it shouldn't be. What are the likely root causes?
gold_facts: by default all pods in a project are reachable from any other pod; a pod becomes non-isolated only once a NetworkPolicy selects it for a given direction, after which only explicitly allowed connections in the union of all selecting policies are permitted

a NetworkPolicy silently doing nothing is almost always either (a) no supporting network plugin implementing NetworkPolicy, or (b) a selector typo -- both fail without an error on the policy object itself, so connectivity must be tested directly
NetworkPolicies are additive: combining multiple policies on the same pods grants the union of what they each allow, not the intersection

question: A PVC has been stuck in Pending for a while and the pod using it is stuck in ContainerCreating waiting for the volume. What should we check?
gold_facts: a PVC with no matching pre-created PV and no viable StorageClass stays Pending indefinitely -- this is the most common storage-request failure mode
if a StorageClass is specified (or a default applies) and no matching PV exists, the class's provisioner dynamically provisions a new PV to satisfy the PVC

a StorageClass with volumeBindingMode: Immediate binds/provisions as soon as the PVC is created, ignoring the consuming pod's scheduling constraints, which can produce unschedulable pods on topology-constrained backends

question: A deployment is failing admission with 'violates PodSecurity... restricted' / 'forbidden pod-security.kubernetes.io' even though its SCC looks correct. Why would PSA still reject it?
gold_facts: PSA (Pod Security Admission) and SCC are two independent controllers enforced in sequence -- the SCC controller mutates/validates the pod first, then the PSA controller validates the (possibly SCC-mutated) pod against the namespace's PSA labels, so a pod can pass SCC admission and still be flagged or rejected by PSA

OpenShift globally enforces the privileged PSA profile and uses restricted only for warn+audit; a synchronization controller auto-sets each namespace's warn/audit labels to the most-privileged profile permitted by the SCCs available to that namespace's ServiceAccounts
manually overriding a synced PSA label disables sync for that label until it is removed or explicitly reconciled

question: Browsers report a TLS certificate mismatch when hitting one of our Routes, and separately we expected a route to be HTTPS-only but it's reachable over plain HTTP. What Route settings control this?
gold_facts: reencrypt routes terminate TLS at the router using the route's own cert/key, then open a NEW separate TLS connection to the pod, and require a destination CA certificate (--dest-ca-cert) so the router trusts the pod's certificate -- a missing/wrong dest CA is a common cause of cert-mismatch errors

edge and reencrypt routes support insecureEdgeTerminationPolicy: None/empty (HTTP disabled) or Redirect (HTTP redirected to HTTPS); a route reachable over HTTP when HTTPS-only was expected likely has this field misconfigured or unset
externalCertificate secrets do not auto-pull a CA bundle -- a tls.caCertificate needed for client auth or re-encryption must be supplied separately

question: A node shows machineconfiguration.openshift.io/state: Degraded with a 'content mismatch for file' reason, and its MachineConfigPool reports NodeDegraded. What caused this and how do we fix it?
gold_facts: the Machine Config Daemon detects configuration drift when on-disk state diverges from the rendered MachineConfig (e.g. an admin hand-edited a file the MachineConfig also manages), and sets both the node and the owning MachineConfigPool to Degraded with a machineconfiguration.openshift.io/reason annotation
a degraded node stays online and serves workloads but cannot be updated further until remediated

remediation is either making the on-disk file/permissions match the MachineConfig again, or forcing a re-apply -- never hand-edit around the mismatch permanently since the next reboot/config change re-detects the same drift

question: An OpenShift cluster upgrade appears stuck -- `oc get co` shows one ClusterOperator with Progressing=True for a long time and the others are waiting. What's the mechanism here?
gold_facts: the CVO organizes manifests into ordered Runlevels and waits until every ClusterOperator in the current runlevel reports Available=True, Degraded=False, and the desired version in status.versions before advancing

a single stuck operator (e.g. kube-apiserver-operator still Progressing=True) blocks the whole upgrade at that runlevel until it resolves, which is why upgrade triage starts with oc get co / oc describe co, not individual pod logs
the Machine Config Operator's manifests apply near the end of the runlevel sequence, so a cluster can report the control plane as updated well before every node finishes draining/rebooting

question: We changed a StorageClass and swapped out the default -- now new PVCs behave differently and some pods that reference specific node selectors are stuck unschedulable after their PVC bound. What settings are in play?
gold_facts: volumeBindingMode: Immediate (the default if unset) binds/provisions as soon as the PVC is created, ignoring the consuming pod's scheduling constraints, which can produce unschedulable pods on topology-constrained backends

WaitForFirstConsumer delays binding/provisioning until a pod actually uses the PVC so the volume honors that pod's node selectors/affinity/taints -- but must not be combined with a pod's nodeName, which bypasses the scheduler and leaves the PVC Pending
exactly one StorageClass is normally marked default via annotation; a PVC with no storageClassName uses it, and changing the cluster default is a supported admin task

question: Our iBGP route reflector clients aren't getting the next-hop we set in an outbound route-map on the RR -- other set clauses seem to work fine internally but this one is being silently dropped for reflected routes. Why?
gold_facts: on reflected routes a route reflector honors only set ip next-hop in an outbound route-map -- most other outbound route-map set clauses are intentionally ignored to avoid loops
next-hop-self should not be used to rewrite next hop on an RR; use an outbound route-map with set ip next-hop instead
Originator-ID and Cluster-list are the two loop-avoidance attributes; single-RR clusters are identified by the RR's router-id, but multiple RRs in one cluster need a shared bgp cluster-id

question: All of our GigE and 10GigE OSPF links show cost 1, so ECMP/best-path selection can't distinguish a 1G backup link from a 10G primary. Also, one neighbor is stuck in EXSTART and never reaches FULL. What's going on?
gold_facts: OSPF cost = auto-cost reference-bandwidth / interface bandwidth, and the default reference is 100 Mbps, so every GigE/10GigE link computes to cost 1 and becomes indistinguishable -- the reference bandwidth must be raised consistently on all routers
hello-interval / dead-interval (dead defaults to 4x hello) must match exactly on a segment or neighbors never reach FULL
MTU mismatch is a classic cause of a neighbor stuck in EXSTART: each router advertises its interface MTU in the DBD packet, and the receiver rejects any DBD advertising a larger MTU than its own

question: A switch port stays 'dead' (not forwarding) for about 30 seconds every time we bring up a link, and separately the wrong switch became the STP root bridge in our topology. What's the mechanism and the fix?
gold_facts: each STP port moves blocking -> listening -> learning -> forwarding, and listening + learning each last one forward-delay (default 15s), so a port takes ~30s to begin forwarding after link-up -- this is the single most common 'port dead after link-up' symptom

the root bridge is elected as the lowest bridge ID (priority + MAC); with everything at the default priority 32768, the lowest MAC wins, so an unintended switch can become root if priorities aren't set

spanning-tree vlan id root primary sets priority to 8192 (or one below the current lowest) and auto-derives timers from network diameter -- set the root deliberately on a backbone/distribution device, never an access switch

question: After a config change our EtherChannel stopped balancing traffic evenly across members, and separately our 1:1 LACP redundant channel isn't fast-switching when a link fails. What's happening in each case?
gold_facts: changing the load-balancing method, or losing the port channel or its last member link, deletes the bucket-to-member mappings (16 hash buckets per port channel); when a link fails its buckets are redistributed round-robin to survivors
LACP 1:1 redundancy requires lacp max-bundle 1 and lacp fast-switchover enabled on BOTH ends, or fast switchover fails
the link with higher port priority (lower numeric value) is active in a 1:1 LACP pair; equal priorities mean there is no revert on recovery

question: Router-originated TCP connections are failing under our local policy-based routing config, but UDP and ICMP from the router work fine. Also, we're worried about the device ARPing forever / blackholing traffic when a PBR next hop goes down. What's the fix for each?
gold_facts: local PBR (ip local policy route-map) applied to router-originated TCP fails unless the device has a RIB/FIB entry for the remote host, even though UDP/ICMP still follow the local policy fine
set ip next-hop verify-availability checks that the next hop is a CDP neighbor before policy-routing, preventing a blackhole/ARP loop when the next hop is down
verify-availability requires CDP and a directly-connected Cisco next hop, and does not work with distributed CEF

question: We ran ISSU on a Catalyst 9500 StackWise Virtual pair. The standby reloaded and rejoined cleanly, but we still got a ~90 second traffic blackhole with OSPF and BGP adjacencies flapping during the switchover. Why, if the ISSU mechanics worked?
gold_facts: the primary cause is that OSPF NSF and BGP Graceful Restart were not configured -- the ISSU reload+switchover worked mechanically, but without NSF/GR the routing protocols tore down adjacencies during the control-plane switchover, withdrawing routes and blackholing traffic until reconvergence

without OSPF NSF, the new active's OSPF process sends Hellos with an empty neighbor list; neighbors see their own Router ID missing and immediately declare the adjacency DOWN, flushing all routes learned from that router

without BGP Graceful Restart, when the TCP session (port 179) drops at switchover, the neighbor immediately withdraws all routes received from that peer; enabling nsf/nsf ietf under OSPF and bgp graceful-restart under BGP lets neighbors keep forwarding on stale routes during a grace period

question: An OSPF adjacency between two routers is permanently stuck in EXSTART and never reaches FULL, even though the physical link shows zero CRC/input errors and BGP between the same pair is Established. What should we check first?
gold_facts: during EXSTART/EXCHANGE each router advertises its interface MTU in the DBD packet header, and the receiver rejects any DBD whose advertised MTU is larger than its own interface MTU, causing the adjacency to loop in EXSTART and never reach FULL
in the diagnosed case, dist-rtr-1 Gi0/1 was set to MTU 9000 (jumbo) while core-1 Gi0/2 was standard MTU 1500 -- a 7500-byte asymmetry across the adjacency link
the fix is to match interface MTU on both ends, or apply ip ospf mtu-ignore on both interfaces to skip the DBD MTU check (masks rather than fixes the mismatch)

question: We bundled a 1G link and a 10G link into the same LACP port-channel and now we're seeing out-of-order packets and throughput that's worse than a single 1G link alone. What's causing this?
gold_facts: Cisco IOS XE does not support mixing link speeds in a single EtherChannel -- all members must have identical speed and duplex; some platforms reject the mismatched member at add-time (%EC_ERR_CFG, member stays suspended/not-in-bundle) while others allow the bundle to form

flow-based load balancing hashes packets into 16 buckets per port-channel; with a 1G and 10G member active, packets from the same flow that land on different-speed links experience ~10x different serialization delay, causing out-of-order delivery at the receiver, which TCP treats as loss and repeatedly halves the congestion window
the fix is either matching member speeds (replace the mismatched link) or putting the 1G uplink in its own separate port-channel -- never bundle unequal-speed links

question: We redistributed OSPF into eBGP but the routes never show up on our eBGP peer, and the ones that do show up have Origin incomplete and an empty AS_Path. What did we miss?
gold_facts: metrics don't translate across protocols -- you must supply a metric via redistribute ospf <pid> metric <n> or default-metric under router bgp, or the route may not be advertised at all
routes redistributed into BGP (including OSPF) have Origin set to incomplete by default, not IGP, which affects best-path selection; a route map can set origin igp to override
redistributed OSPF routes have an empty AS_Path since they originate in your own AS, and carry no AS_Path prepend unless explicitly configured with set as-path prepend

question: After removing 'no redistribute isis' from our BGP config we found redistribution had stopped working entirely, and separately routes are being redistributed in a loop between two protocols. What's the root cause of each?
gold_facts: 'no redistribute' is protocol-specific: it is subtractive under BGP/OSPF/RIP (removes only the named keyword), but no redistribute isis (and no redistribute eigrp from EIGRP rel5 onward) removes the entire redistribute command
a route map with no match clause matches everything and with no set clause modifies nothing -- redistribution loops typically come from not filtering inbound consistently
because metrics don't translate across protocols, redistributing between two OSPF processes does not preserve OSPF metrics either, which is a related but distinct trap

question: If I want to use token exchange, do I need to enable a preview feature flag, or is it on by default?

In RHBK 26.6, it split into standard token exchange V2 (fully supported, enabled by default) and legacy token exchange V1 (preview, deprecated, off by default, requires FGAP v1)

question: Can I run custom JavaScript authenticators/mappers in RHBK without any special feature flag, or is that still gated?

question: Can I configure the Keycloak CR's telemetry settings with a first-class spec.telemetry field, or do I have to fall back to additionalOptions?

question: Does the Keycloak Operator support rolling updates for patch releases automatically, or do I need to opt into an experimental feature?

question: For fine-grained admin permissions, is FGAP v1 or v2 the default/supported version, and does that matter for features like legacy token exchange?
